d.d: An astringent salt, usually occurring in the form of pale crystals, much used in the dyeing and tanning trade and in certain medicines, and now understood to be a double sulphate of potassium and aluminium (K₂SO₄·Al₂(SO₄)₃·24H₂O).
Any similar double sulphate in which either or both of the potassium and aluminium is wholly or partly replaced by other univalent or tervalent cations.
A past attendee or graduate (of any gender) of a college, university or other educational institution.
To steep in, or otherwise impregnate with, a solution of alum; to treat with alum.
Aluminum oxide, especially when used in mining, material sciences or ceramics, a refractory solid compound.
A light, silvery metal extracted from bauxite, and a chemical element (symbol Al) with an atomic number of 13.
American, Canadian, and Philippines standard spelling of aluminium.
A female pupil or student (especially of a university or college).

d.x: The alumni of this university include many famous artists and politicians.
